cues.title: The implemented core
cues.note: We built the browser workflow and a deterministic JavaScript rule core. Theatre plans, device state, usage history and alarms become structured inputs.

cues.title: Reject first
cues.note: First, reject collisions, thin data, motion updates, unavailable people and missing backup. Missing information never means a free machine.

cues.title: Rank what survives
cues.note: The team’s scorer then ranks legal windows using unplanned use, emergency demand and case overrun. These inputs are synthetic; clinical calibration is still ahead.

cues.title: An inspectable result
cues.note: The result names the device, window and replacement. An explanation can describe that result. It cannot relax the rules.

cues.title: Device in use
cues.note: This is the actual start predicate. A device in use blocks the proposal.

cues.title: Emergency alarm
cues.note: An alarm closes the gate, even when the rest looks ready.

cues.title: Package recalled
cues.note: A recalled package also blocks it. A persuasive explanation changes nothing.

cues.title: Eligible is not started
cues.note: All checks pass? The gate becomes eligible. A human still confirms the start. [The active button can start this browser simulation; it controls no device.]

cues.title: The proposed pilot stack
cues.note: Around that core, our proposed hospital node uses Python and FastAPI, SQLite for local state, and server-sent events for the browser. Local rules keep working without a language model.

cues.title: An approved package route
cues.note: The node initiates an approved connection to teamplay Fleet and remote services. Packages come inward; permitted technical status goes back.

cues.title: Transport, not trust
cues.note: The robot adapter uses the proposed ROS 2 and Nav2 layer. It carries power and approved data to one device. The handoff is not a network bridge.

cues.title: Close the loop
cues.note: Status and logs return to the hospital node. Exceptions go to a responsible person. Device-side interfaces and power engineering still need validation with Siemens.

cues.title: Bind the permission
cues.note: The proposed authorization contract binds a person, a device, a package and a plan version. Manufacturer signatures establish package origin; hospital identity establishes permission.

cues.title: Invalidate the old decision
cues.note: Change the window, recall the package or lose current readiness, and the old permission cannot authorize a new start.

cues.title: Run the invariants
cues.note: These checks run against the same code on this page. Cases stay protected. Unknown data stays unknown. Alarms block. Replayed inputs reproduce the decision.

cues.title: The next engineering step
cues.note: The next step is a validated hospital adapter and physical handoff, with the decision record preserved from proposal to returned result.

cues.title: Accountable by design
cues.note: An explainable plan. An accountable handoff.

checks: Blocked gate disables button; trusted human click starts only eligible local simulation; reset clears it
